nodes.description: Insulin action is severely impaired. Compensatory hyperinsulinemia may initially preserve glucose tolerance; diabetes develops when compensation is inadequate. Lipid and leptin pathways contribute through incompletely resolved intermediates.

evidence.reference_title: AGPAT2 is mutated in congenital generalized lipodystrophy linked to chromosome 9q34.
evidence.snippet: Congenital generalized lipodystrophy is an autosomal recessive disorder characterized by marked paucity of adipose tissue, extreme insulin resistance, hypertriglyceridemia, hepatic steatosis and early onset of diabetes.

nodes.description: Fibrates and long-chain omega-3 fatty acids are used for severe hypertriglyceridemia. Their use in lipodystrophy is supported mainly by clinical experience. Consider myopathy risk, particularly in CGL4.

evidence.reference_title: The Diagnosis and Management of Lipodystrophy Syndromes: A Multi-Society Practice Guideline.
evidence.snippet: Fibrates and/or long-chain omega-3 fatty acids should be used for triglycerides >500 mg/dL and may be considered for triglycerides >200 mg/dL.

nodes.description: Bscl2-deficient mouse-derived cells show excessive cAMP/PKA-dependent lipolysis during differentiation.

evidence.reference_title: Berardinelli-seip congenital lipodystrophy 2/seipin is a cell-autonomous regulator of lipolysis essential for adipocyte differentiation.
evidence.snippet: In vitro differentiation of both Bscl2(-/-) murine embryonic fibroblasts (MEFs) and stromal vascular cells (SVCs) reveals normal early-phase adipocyte differentiation but a striking failure in terminal differentiation due to unbridled cyclic AMP (cAMP)-dependent protein kinase A (PKA)-activated lipolysis, which leads to loss of lipid droplets and silencing of the expression of adipose tissue-specific transcription factors.
